page: Microsoft Azure E32pds_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine powered by a 32-core Microsoft Neoverse-N2 ARM processor running at 3.4 GHz. Built on the arm64 architecture, this server features 32 dedicated physical cores with a single thread per core, eliminating hyperthreading overhead. It is equipped with 256.0 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. Storage is bundled as a local 1890 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance is capable of utilizing Premium Storage. The CPU cache configuration includes 64 KB L1d cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 128 MB L3 cache.

Benchmark results indicate top-tier memory performance, with uncached large-block read bandwidth reaching 449.0 GB/sec and write bandwidth at 188.31 GB/sec, both placing in the top 10% tier. PassMark database operations and memory scores also rank in the top tier. Multi-core CPU performance is strong, as demonstrated by a Geekbench multi-core score of 20088.0 and a stress-ng multi-core score of 66297.85. The server also exhibits strong capabilities in Redis SET operations, achieving 61.82 million operations per second, and static web serving throughput at 56.14 GB/sec.

Despite strong multi-core and memory capabilities, single-core performance remains in the average tier, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1693.0. The ARM architecture lacks AVX and AMX instruction sets, which limits its suitability for certain vector-heavy workloads. This is reflected in the poor prompt processing speed of 4.65 tokens per second for large 70B LLM models, though text generation for the same model remains average. Given its high memory density, fast local NVMe storage, and top-tier database benchmark results, the E32pds_v6 is highly efficient for memory-intensive workloads, database hosting, Redis caching, and software compilation.
